name: Belial
title: Personification of evil and lawlessness
summary: Belial is not a specific historical figure in the Bible, but a term and personification of evil, lawlessness, and worthlessness. In the Old Testament, the expression "sons of Belial" or "men of Belial" refers to wicked and ungodly people. In the New Testament, Paul mentions Belial as a contrast to Christ, and in intertestamental times the term was understood as a name for Satan or a demonic figure.

keyEvents.title: Sons of Belial in Gibeah
keyEvents.description: Men in Gibeah, referred to as "sons of Belial," committed horrific acts against a Levite's concubine, leading to a civil war against the tribe of Benjamin.

keyEvents.title: The Wickedness of Eli's Sons
keyEvents.description: Hophni and Phinehas, the sons of the priest Eli, were called "sons of Belial" because they did not know the Lord and dishonored the sacrificial service.

keyEvents.title: Nabal Referred to as a Man of Belial
keyEvents.description: Abigail described her husband Nabal as a man of Belial—an foolish and wicked person who refused to help David.

keyEvents.title: False Witnesses Against Naboth
keyEvents.description: Queen Jezebel arranged for two men of Belial to give false testimony against Naboth, so that he was stoned to death and King Ahab could take his vineyard.

keyEvents.title: Men of Belial Against David
keyEvents.description: After the victory over the Amalekites, wicked men, referred to as "men of Belial", refused to share the plunder with those who had stayed behind with the equipment. David rejected this and established equal distribution.

keyEvents.title: Paul sets Belial against Christ
keyEvents.description: In his second letter to the Corinthians, Paul uses Belial as a direct contrast to Christ, warning against fellowship between light and darkness, believers and unbelievers.
